outcome: The problem (the asymptotic growth rate of wasted space W(x)) remains open, but the rigorously-established upper bound moved during the window: Chung and Graham's 2019 claim of W(x)=O(x^0.6) was discovered in 2025 (Arslanov & Bui) to contain a calculation error, temporarily reverting the proven state of the art to the weaker W(x)=O(x^{(3+sqrt(2))/7} log x); two independent papers then re-established W(x)=O(x^0.6) rigorously by new methods (Bui, Aug 2025; McClenagan, preprinted Feb 2026 from a 2024 thesis). A third paper (Bui, Apr 2025) simplified the Roth-Vaughan lower-bound proof technique without changing the bound. No AI system was involved in any of this work.

disputes.summary: Bui (arXiv:2508.04603, submitted 2025-08-06, v2 2026-03-15) and McClenagan (arXiv:2602.01484, submitted 2026-02-01) independently proved the same bound W(x)=O(x^{3/5}) (equivalently O(x^0.6)) by different constructions. McClenagan's result derives from his 2024 UNBC master's thesis (DOI 10.24124/2024/59553); the arXiv writeup itself states that 'since submission [of the thesis], a similar result by a different method was published in 2025 (arXiv:2508.04603 by Bui),' i.e. McClenagan's own account places his result first but its public arXiv posting second. I could not establish the exact month of the 2024 thesis defense/deposit, so I cannot determine whether the thesis itself was completed before or after the 26 January 2024 cutoff.

summary: The Wikipedia bullet as frozen on 26 Jan 2024 is bare ('what is the asymptotic growth rate of wasted space?'), with no bound cited. Checking the frozen revision confirms this. The problem itself -- the precise asymptotic growth rate of W(x) -- remains fully open; nothing in the window resolves it or narrows it to a single answer. What happened in the window concerns the best known *upper* bound, and it is more complicated than the triage summary suggested: Chung and Graham had claimed in a 2019 paper (Discrete & Comput. Geom. 64(3):690-699) that W(x)=O(x^0.6) (equivalently x^{3/5}), improving on Wang et al. (2016)'s O(x^0.625). As best I can tell from later sources, this claim was the believed state of the art as of January 2024. In 2025, Arslanov and Bui (Discrete & Comput. Geom., DOI 10.1007/s00454-025-00767-w) identified a technical error in Chung-Graham's calculation of a quantity W_5, invalidating the 2019 proof and reverting the rigorously-established bound to the earlier, weaker W(x)=O(x^{(3+sqrt(2))/7} log x) (Chung-Graham 2009). Two papers then closed this gap independently: Hong Duc Bui (arXiv:2508.04603, first submitted 2025-08-06) gave a new construction rigorously proving W(x)=O(x^0.6); Rory McClenagan (arXiv:2602.01484, submitted 2026-02-01, extracted from a 2024 master's thesis) gave a different construction (via 'stacks' of unit squares plus trapezoidal sub-packings) proving the same bound, explicitly framing the result as confirming that 'the bound claimed by Chung and Graham... is, in fact, correct, using a new algorithm.' A third paper, Bui (arXiv:2504.09489, submitted 2025-04-13, presented at CCCG 2025), proved that only 'good squares' (inclination <= 10^-10) need be considered when establishing the Roth-Vaughan lower bound W(x) not-in o(x^{1/2}), simplifying that proof's case analysis without changing the bound itself -- this is `progress` on proof technique, not a moved bound, and by itself would not change status. I read all three papers (HTML/PDF) in full or via careful extraction, including abstracts, introductions, and acknowledgements, and found no mention anywhere of AI, machine learning, neural networks, computer search, or automated/computer-assisted proof techniques; the acknowledgements in the two substantive papers thank a human proofreader and anonymous reviewers only. I classify the overall status as `progress` rather than `partial` or `resolved`: no case or sub-instance of the open growth-rate question was settled, and the open problem (the exact asymptotic rate) is untouched; what moved is the best known upper bound, which is exactly the `progress` category, and I use the Bui paper's 2025-08-06 submission as the dated event since it is the first public written argument re-establishing O(x^0.6) rigorously (McClenagan's underlying thesis may predate this, but I could not establish its month, and its own arXiv writeup postdates Bui's). `resolution_direction` is `confirmed` because the re-proof confirms (rather than refutes) the previously-believed-but-then-invalidated Chung-Graham bound.
competing_reading: One could argue this is `open_stale`-adjacent: the O(x^0.6) bound was already the publicly believed state of the art before the frozen revision date, so the 2025-2026 papers merely repair a gap rather than advance genuinely new mathematics beyond what was already assumed true in January 2024. Under that reading the 'progress' is illusory -- the field is only catching back up to where everyone already thought it was. I did not adopt this reading because between the January 2019 claim and the 2025 papers there was a period (starting with the 2025 Arslanov-Bui erratum) where the rigorously-known bound was strictly worse than O(x^0.6), and restoring a result after a genuine, published invalidation is itself a real mathematical event (a new, different, correct proof was required, not a correction of the old one) rather than a non-event. A second, narrower competing reading: the Bui 'good squares' paper (2504.09489) could be read as `partial` if one considers the reduction to good-square packings itself a nontrivial partial characterization result rather than pure proof-simplification, but the paper's own framing ('allows the lower bound proof... to be simplified') supports treating it as technique-simplification, which does not by itself change `status`.
what_would_settle_it: The exact month (or day) of deposit/defense of McClenagan's 2024 UNBC thesis (DOI 10.24124/2024/59553) would settle whether an argument for W(x)=O(x^0.6) existed publicly before or after 26 January 2024, which would matter if the thesis itself (as opposed to its 2026 arXiv writeup) counts as the first public written argument. It would not change the `progress` classification (the open problem itself is untouched either way) but could shift the `event` date earlier and add nuance to the `open_stale` question for the upper-bound sub-thread.

events.what: Arslanov and Bui identify an error in Chung-Graham's 2019 calculation of W_5, invalidating the claimed O(x^0.6) bound and reverting the rigorous bound to O(x^{(3+sqrt(2))/7} log x)
Bui shows only 'good squares' need be considered for the Roth-Vaughan lower bound, simplifying its proof without changing the bound
Bui gives a new construction rigorously proving W(x)=O(x^0.6)
McClenagan independently proves W(x)=O(x^0.6) by a different construction (2024 UNBC master's thesis; arXiv writeup 2026-02-01)

judgement.doubts: Whether this is movement at all is debatable: O(x^0.6) was the published, believed bound (Chung-Graham 2019) at the snapshot, so the 2025-26 work restores rather than advances the believed frontier; relative to the rigorously established bound after the 2025 erratum it is a moved bound, so progress is kept. McClenagan's thesis is dated only to 2024 and cannot be placed either side of 26 January 2024; a thesis approved by a committee would count as digested, but either way the tier is progress.
